questions.question: How many core verb tenses does English have when combining time (past/present/future) with aspect?
questions.explanation: Three times (past, present, future) combined with four aspects (simple, continuous, perfect, perfect continuous) give twelve core tenses.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect correctly?
options: I have lived here for five years.
I have seen that film yesterday.
questions.explanation: Present perfect connects past and present without a specific time: "I have lived here for five years." With "yesterday" you must use past simple.

questions.question: Why is "I am loving this song" considered incorrect in standard English grammar?
options: "Love" is a stative verb and is not normally used in continuous form
Continuous forms only exist in the past
questions.explanation: Stative verbs like know, love, believe, want and own describe states, not actions, and are not normally used in the continuous form.

questions.question: Which tense is described as the "past of the past"?
questions.explanation: The past perfect ("I had walked") describes an action completed before another point in the past.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly describes a background action in the past?
options: I was walking home when it started to rain.
I walk home when it started to rain.
I have walked home when it started to rain.
I will walk home when it started to rain.
questions.explanation: Past continuous ("was walking") sets the background scene, and past simple ("started") marks the interrupting event.
